study_design: Ecological cross-country correlation study of national food supply and cancer incidence and mortality rates
reason: The study correlates national dietary supply with overall prostatic cancer incidence and mortality rates. It does not analyze an aggressive incident prostate cancer endpoint; prostate cancer mortality is also not presented as lethal incidence in an initially cancer-free cohort.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Concerning prostatic cancer, milk (1961-90) was most closely correlated (r = 0.711) with its incidence, followed by meat and coffee.
estimate_classifications.reason: This ecological association concerns overall prostatic cancer incidence, not aggressive incidence.
